vision_report.narrative_description: As the Garden Botanical Observer, I performed a meticulous audit of the chronological image sequence. The primary challenge was the inconsistent lighting, with images T-2 and CURRENT being almost entirely dark, severely limiting visual assessment. However, for the images with sufficient visibility (EARLIEST, T-5, T-4, T-3, T-1), both the P2 Mexican Mint and the Unmonitored Money Plant consistently exhibit signs of good health. The Mexican Mint in the black pot maintains light green, turgid leaves, and the soil appears adequately moist. The Money Plant in the white cup, undergoing water propagation, shows a healthy, dark green, turgid leaf. No signs of wilting, discoloration, pest damage, or incidental growth (weeds, moss) were observed in any visible image. The biome saw the introduction of a white cylindrical object in T-1, which was not clearly visible in CURRENT, and a new faint red object in CURRENT. Despite the intermittent visual obstructions, the visible data suggests both plants are maintaining stable health, with no visual evidence of decline over the observed period.
